newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate pares rise on liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate pares rise on liquidity.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates moderated earlier increased to close up 50 basis points at 22.50 percent on Friday on ample liquidity after a calm session, traders said.
"Not much happened, the (central bank) auctions came as expected, and were assigned at expected rates," a trader said.
Overnight Cetes rates had opened at a session high of 23.30 percent.
Traders said a slight fall in U.S. long bond yields enhanced stability in the local money market.
Yields on 30-year U.S. Treasury bonds declined to 6.95 percent from 6.96 percent following a stronger-then-expected fall in U.S. producer price data in early trade.
Banco de Mexico drained liquidity of 2.604 billion pesos from the system through five auctions which it assigned at rates of between 24.75-24.30 percent.
Overnight rates on bank paper ended down 85 basis points at 24.00 percent.

Traders said secondary interest rates could come under pressure next week from the Federal Open Market Committee meeting on March 25 to review interest U.S. interest rates which could "make waves", they said.
Forthcoming Easter vacations could also squeeze liquidity and put rates under pressure, they added.
"The end of the month is coming up and that could lead to some uncertainty, coupled with the fact we cannot yet rule out a hike in U.S. interest rates," another trader said.
Liquidity of 1.080 billion pesos was slated to return to the system from prior central bank intervention on Monday. ((--Elena Vega, Mexico City newsroom +525 728-9554))
